name: Alex Cotton
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember changing a name on a boat that had never moved.” Monday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Alex pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I want the name painted over. It's my mother's name and she wants it back for her own dinghy.
appearance: Alex has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a brown corduroy jacket. It usually goes with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. When somebody else has the floor, Alex rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Alex is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Alex is concerned.
agenda: To reclaim the mother's name for her own dinghy.
family: Ari Pennrose is Alex’s half-sibling. Alex is free to hang up first. Ari makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The porch light*, Ari says, “I used that lit window in a slide about waste.”
connections: Elinor Stein. The family may separate the little dinghy from the larger boat's borrowed name.

reactions.situation: The boat's owners give two answers about selling
reactions.response: Alex asks both owners which decision has actually been made.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Alex asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.
